# CRW-895: find -delete, find -exec/-execdir/-ok/-okdir and xargs/parallel deletions, as the issue and the 10-09 re-check list them.
# ../repo is the managed checkout itself, .. is the slot root (an ancestor). Format: see shellwrite_repro_test.go.

=== CRW-895-a1 | R
--why The issue: find -delete on the checkout itself with no test before the action.
find ../repo -delete

=== CRW-895-a2 | R
--why The issue: find from the slot root (an ancestor) runs rm -rf on what it finds.
find .. -maxdepth 0 -name repo -exec rm -rf {} +

=== CRW-895-a3 | R
--why The issue: xargs rm -rf with the checkout named on the left of the pipe.
echo ../repo | xargs rm -rf

=== CRW-895-a4 | U
--why The issue: find "$PWD" -exec rm -rf. $PWD is not a known word, so the reader refuses it in every gate (the worktree guard denies, as the issue asks).
find "$PWD" -exec rm -rf {} +

=== CRW-895-a5 | R
--why The issue: find from the slot root deletes with no test.
find .. -delete

=== CRW-895-a6 | R
--why The issue: printf names the checkout for xargs rm -rf.
printf '%s\n' ../repo | xargs rm -rf

=== CRW-895-a7 | R
--why The issue: an unreadable left side (a variable) fails closed, with a non-recursive rm too.
echo "$X" | xargs rm

=== CRW-895-a7b | R
--why The same with rm -rf.
echo "$X" | xargs rm -rf

=== CRW-895-c1 | B
--why The issue control: a start equal to the worktree with a test before the action.
find . -name '*.o' -delete

=== CRW-895-c2 | B
--why The issue control: a start inside the worktree.
find build -delete

=== CRW-895-c3 | B
--why The issue control: a test before a non-recursive rm.
find . -type f -name '*.tmp' -exec rm {} +

=== CRW-895-c4 | B
--why The issue control: a find list is not a named path.
find . -name '*.o' | xargs rm

=== CRW-895-c5 | B
--why The issue control, exactly as the issue body spells it (with -f).
git ls-files -z | xargs -0 rm -f

=== CRW-895-c5b | B
--why The issue body control without -f (the independent verifier).
git ls-files -z | xargs -0 rm

=== CRW-895-c6 | B
--why The issue control: ls lists names the guard does not read.
ls | xargs rm

=== CRW-895-c7 | B
--why find . -type f -delete: a -type test comes before the action (the 10-09 re-check).
find . -type f -delete

=== CRW-895-c8 | B
--why A -newer test before -delete.
find . -newer x -delete

=== CRW-895-c9 | B
--why A -path test before -delete with the checkout spelled ../repo.
find ../repo -path '*/build/*' -delete

=== CRW-895-c10 | B
--why A test before -delete with the absolute checkout path.
find {CHECKOUT} -name '*.o' -delete

=== CRW-895-c11 | B
--why A parenthesised test group before the action.
find . \( -name '*.o' -o -name '*.a' \) -delete

=== CRW-895-c12 | B
--why A negated test before the action.
find . ! -name keep -delete

=== CRW-895-c13 | B
--why -execdir after a test.
find . -name '*.tmp' -execdir rm {} +

=== CRW-895-c14 | B
--why A start under the worktree with rmdir.
find build -empty -exec rmdir {} +

=== CRW-895-c15 | B
--why Names inside the worktree are not the worktree.
echo build ../repo/build | xargs rm

=== CRW-895-c16 | B
--why The current directory spelled . is allowed (the issue rule excepts it).
echo . | xargs rm

=== CRW-895-c17 | B
--why find that only prints is not a deletion.
find .. -name repo -print

=== CRW-895-c18 | B
--why find -exec of a program that does not delete.
find .. -exec ls {} +

=== CRW-895-c19 | B
--why xargs with a program that does not delete.
echo ../repo | xargs ls

=== CRW-895-c20 | B
--why xargs rm with the operand in the command and no named left side.
xargs rm ./build

=== CRW-895-c21 | B
--why Standard input from /dev/null names nothing.
xargs rm < /dev/null

=== CRW-895-c22 | B
--why Names of a sibling directory of the checkout.
echo ../other | xargs rm

=== CRW-895-c23 | B | deviation=none/allow/deny
--why A test before the action with a find option in front of the start.
find -L . -name '*.o' -delete

=== CRW-895-c24 | B
--why A pattern that spells -delete is the argument of -name, not an action.
find . -name -delete

=== CRW-895-d1 | R
--why The 10-09 re-check: -exec rmdir from the slot root (an ancestor).
find .. -exec rmdir {} +

=== CRW-895-d2 | R
--why The 10-09 re-check: -exec shred on the checkout with no test.
find ../repo -exec shred {} +

=== CRW-895-d3 | R
--why The 10-09 re-check: -exec unlink on the checkout with no test.
find ../repo -exec unlink {} \;

=== CRW-895-d4 | R
--why The 10-09 re-check (real impact): -exec git worktree remove on the checkout.
find ../repo -exec git worktree remove {} \;

=== CRW-895-d5 | R
--why The independent verifier: -okdir is a listed action.
find ../repo -okdir rm -rf {} \;

=== CRW-895-d6 | R
--why -execdir rm -rf with the checkout and no test.
find ../repo -execdir rm -rf {} +

=== CRW-895-d7 | R
--why -ok rm -rf with the checkout and no test.
find ../repo -ok rm -rf {} \;

=== CRW-895-d8 | R
--why -exec with a non-recursive rm and the checkout with no test.
find ../repo -exec rm {} +

=== CRW-895-d9 | R
--why A test does not help when the start is an ancestor.
find .. -name repo -exec rm {} +

=== CRW-895-d10 | R
--why The absolute slot root as the start with a -name test.
find {CHECKOUT}/.. -name repo -delete

=== CRW-895-d11 | R
--why An option before the start must not hide it.
find -L ../repo -delete

=== CRW-895-d12 | R
--why After -o the -delete is reached without the test.
find ../repo -name a -o -delete

=== CRW-895-d13 | R
--why The current directory with no test.
find . -exec rm {} +

=== CRW-895-d14 | R
--why -execdir git worktree remove from an ancestor.
find .. -name repo -execdir git worktree remove {} \;

=== CRW-895-d15 | R
--why git -C before worktree remove under find.
find ../repo -exec git -C .. worktree remove {} \;

=== CRW-895-d16 | R
--why The absolute checkout path with no test and -exec rmdir.
find {CHECKOUT} -exec rmdir {} +

=== CRW-895-d17 | R
--why Two starts, the second is the checkout.
find build ../repo -delete

=== CRW-895-d18 | R
--why find with the here-string and -delete (CRW-1011 shape) with the slot root.
find .. <<<x -delete

=== CRW-895-e1 | R
--why The 10-09 re-check (real impact): xargs git worktree remove with the checkout on the left.
echo ../repo | xargs git worktree remove

=== CRW-895-e2 | R
--why xargs rm (non-recursive) with the checkout on the left.
echo ../repo | xargs rm

=== CRW-895-e3 | R
--why xargs rmdir (the independent verifier).
echo ../repo | xargs rmdir

=== CRW-895-e4 | R
--why xargs unlink with the checkout on the left.
echo ../repo | xargs unlink

=== CRW-895-e5 | R
--why xargs shred with the checkout on the left.
echo ../repo | xargs shred

=== CRW-895-e6 | R
--why An unreadable left side from a command substitution (the independent verifier).
echo "$(cat list.txt)" | xargs rm

=== CRW-895-e7 | R
--why ~ is the home, a spelling that is not . (the independent verifier); the tilde is not a known word.
echo ~ | xargs rm

=== CRW-895-e8 | R
--why xargs -a reads the names from a file: unreadable.
xargs -a list.txt rm

=== CRW-895-e9 | R
--why A here-string names the checkout.
xargs rm <<< ../repo

=== CRW-895-e10 | R
--why A here-document names the checkout.
xargs rm << EOF
../repo
EOF

=== CRW-895-e11 | R
--why The absolute checkout path on the left.
echo {CHECKOUT} | xargs rm

=== CRW-895-e12 | R
--why The slot root is an ancestor.
echo .. | xargs rm

=== CRW-895-e13 | R
--why printf with a backslash-n inside one word.
printf '../repo\n' | xargs rm

=== CRW-895-e14 | R
--why printf with NUL separators and xargs -0.
printf '../repo\0' | xargs -0 rm

=== CRW-895-e15 | R
--why xargs -I with a replacement string.
echo ../repo | xargs -I{} rm {}

=== CRW-895-e16 | R
--why cat passes the pipe through.
echo ../repo | cat | xargs rm

=== CRW-895-e17 | R
--why $PWD is not a known word.
echo $PWD | xargs rm

=== CRW-895-e18 | R
--why Standard input from a file is unreadable (the same as -a).
xargs rm < list.txt

=== CRW-895-e19 | R
--why The checkout with a trailing dot segment is still the checkout.
echo ../repo/. | xargs rm

=== CRW-895-e20 | R
--why A second name on the line.
echo build ../repo | xargs rmdir

=== CRW-895-e21 | R
--why A file list that find prints from the checkout start is the checkout.
find ../repo -type f | xargs rm

=== CRW-895-e22 | R
--why sed rewrites a known list into names the guard cannot read.
echo build | sed s/build/../repo/ | xargs rm

=== CRW-895-e23 | R
--why A subshell producer is not read.
(echo ../repo) | xargs rm

=== CRW-895-e24 | R
--why xargs git worktree remove with a here-string.
xargs git worktree remove <<< {CHECKOUT}

=== CRW-895-e25 | R
--why A nested sh -c carries the pipe: xargs sh -c with rm and the placeholder.
echo ../repo | xargs -I{} sh -c 'rm {}'

=== CRW-895-e26 | R
--why nohup echo carries the words.
nohup echo ../repo | xargs rm

=== CRW-895-e27 | R
--why cat with a here-document names the checkout.
cat << EOF | xargs rm
../repo
EOF

=== CRW-895-p1 | U
--why parallel runs the program its operands name at run time: unreadable in every gate (the independent verifier: git worktree remove).
echo ../repo | parallel git worktree remove

=== CRW-895-p2 | U
--why parallel rmdir.
echo ../repo | parallel rmdir

=== CRW-895-p3 | U
--why parallel unlink.
echo ../repo | parallel unlink

=== CRW-895-p4 | U
--why parallel shred.
echo ../repo | parallel shred

=== CRW-895-p5 | U
--why parallel rm -rf.
echo ../repo | parallel rm -rf

=== CRW-895-p6 | U
--why parallel rm with a safe left side is refused too (the reader does not model parallel; an accepted over-refusal).
ls | parallel rm

=== CRW-895-c25 | B
--why A prune branch before the action: every path to -delete passes a test.
find ../repo -type d -name build -prune -o -type f -delete

=== CRW-895-c26 | B
--why git -C with a subcommand that removes nothing.
echo repo | xargs git -C .. status

=== CRW-895-c27 | B
--why The names ls prints are the contents of the checkout, not the checkout.
ls ../repo | xargs rmdir

=== CRW-895-c28 | B
--why A file the producer reads is output the text does not name (cat is a plain command; xargs -a and < FILE are the unreadable forms).
cat list.txt | xargs rm

=== CRW-895-c29 | B
--why A relative name in the current directory is not the checkout.
xargs git worktree remove <<< repo

=== CRW-895-c30 | B
--why A test group in which every alternative holds a test.
find ../repo \( -name '*.o' -o -name '*.a' \) -delete

=== CRW-895-e28 | R
--why tee passes the list on.
echo ../repo | tee x | xargs rmdir

=== CRW-895-e29 | R
--why sort and uniq pass the list on.
echo ../repo | sort | uniq | xargs rmdir

=== CRW-895-e30 | R
--why sed rewrites a known list into names the guard cannot read.
echo ../repo | sed s/a/b/ | xargs rmdir

=== CRW-895-e31 | R
--why cut rewrites a known list.
echo ../repo | cut -d, -f1 | xargs rmdir

=== CRW-895-e32 | R
--why git -C .. moves the directory the name is resolved from.
xargs git -C .. worktree remove <<< repo

=== CRW-895-e33 | R
--why A name relative to a directory the text changed to.
cd ..; echo repo | xargs rmdir

=== CRW-895-e34 | R
--why env runs xargs; the pipe still feeds it.
echo ../repo | env xargs rmdir

=== CRW-895-e35 | R
--why xargs runs env, which runs the removal.
echo ../repo | xargs env rmdir

=== CRW-895-e36 | R
--why A subshell carries the pipe.
echo ../repo | (xargs rmdir)

=== CRW-895-e37 | R
--why A function that prints the checkout feeds the pipe.
f() { echo ../repo; }; f | xargs rmdir

=== CRW-895-e38 | R
--why find lists the checkout (its start point) for a non-recursive removal that can remove a worktree.
find .. -maxdepth 1 -name repo | xargs git worktree remove

=== CRW-895-d19 | R
--why sh -c in -exec runs the removal with the placeholder.
find ../repo -exec sh -c 'rm "$1"' _ {} \;

=== CRW-895-d20 | R
--why The slot root among several start points.
find .. . -name x -delete

=== CRW-895-d21 | R
--why -H before the start does not hide it.
find -H .. -name x -delete

=== CRW-895-d22 | R
--why An option that takes a value (-D) before the start does not hide it.
find -D tree .. -name x -delete

=== CRW-895-d23 | R
--why A group with an always-true alternative guards nothing.
find ../repo \( -name x -o -true \) -delete

=== CRW-895-d24 | R
--why -prune before -o leaves -delete without a test.
find ../repo -name x -prune -o -delete

=== CRW-895-d25 | R
--why No start point means the current directory, which is the checkout.
find -delete
